what_this_is: Nine paired interleaved repeats of ctx128-c32 -- control against the shipped `persist` policy, nothing else -- because three repeats of that cell drove the first full TTF-1 receipt to -99.5% and three repeats cannot say whether that was the policy or the box. The generation allows nine. This spends them on one cell.

findings.finding: The unexplained c=32 collapse recurred, and this run diagnoses it.
findings.detail:
Repeat 1's candidate returned 575.1 tok/s against its own median of 893.0 -- a 36% drop, the failure this repository has carried as open since 0.1 and has never had a mechanism for. Every guard passes it: all requests completed, 63 of 64 decode steps took the packed path at 32 rows, the hook applied a policy, and no capture was invalidated.

The adapter's own step counters say what happened. Eight of the nine runs bracketed 78 steps, of which 63 were batched decode; the collapsed one bracketed 207, of which 63 were batched decode. THE DECODE WORK WAS IDENTICAL. What differs is 144 single-row steps against 15, and 15 geometry rebuilds against 5 -- the engine recompiles whenever the in-flight sequence count changes, so fifteen rebuilds is a run whose concurrency never settled. The runtime scheduled the 32 requests substantially serially: the wall time grew while the batched work did not, and aggregate throughput is tokens over wall time.

The signature separates cleanly. Across the 138 measured records with telemetry taken on this box today -- three matrices, 77 hooked runs -- every healthy group's non-decode step count is stable to within one step (77, 77, 77 at ctx128-c1; 15, 15, 15 at ctx128-c16; 16, 16, 16 at ctx128-c4) and exactly one run deviates, at 9.6x its group's median. `eval/frontier/runner.py::scheduling_outliers` flags it and nothing else, and `eval/test_frontier.py` pins the nine measured numbers.

It is REPORTED, never refused. The failure is the runtime's, it lands on whichever arm happens to be running, and turning it into a cell failure would charge a candidate for it. What an operator needs to know is that a median over nine repeats survives one of these and a median over three does not -- which is the same conclusion the rest of this file reaches from the other direction.

findings.finding: Goodput: a resolved regression of about 1.2%, nine pairs out of nine.
findings.detail: Every one of the nine paired repeats is negative, median -1.20%. A paired sign test over nine pairs all in one direction is p = 0.004 two-sided, and pairing is exactly what the interleaving exists to enable. Note the other reading: that cell's PUBLISHED control spread is 1.738% peak-to-peak, so -1.2% does not clear the peak-to-peak rule this repository applies elsewhere. Both are reported. The sign test is the stronger statistic here and the peak-to-peak rule is the more conservative one.
findings.caveat: Repeat 1's candidate came in at 575.1 tok/s against 901.2 -- a -36% collapse in the opening pair, which is the warm-up effect eval/real_eval.py documents and offers --discard-leading for, defaulted to zero so every published result stays reproducible. Excluding it the median is -1.12% and eight of eight are still negative.

findings.finding: p99 inter-token latency: NOT resolved at nine repeats, and the three-repeat figure was sampling.
findings.detail:
The first full matrix reported a p99 of 133.97 ms against a control's 47.30 over three repeats -- a 183% regression -- and docs/VERDICT.md reported it as a real distributional change. Nine repeats do not support that. The paired ratio is worse for the candidate in SEVEN of nine pairs with a median of 1.083, which a sign test puts at p ~ 0.18. The cell's published control spread on this objective is 481% and the control's own nine values span 45.1 to 240.1 ms, which is 432%: the calibration was right and three repeats sampled it.

The mechanism is visible in the pairs. Every run carries one very long gap -- the generation's long-prefill request landing on a decode step -- at around 673 ms, and with 2016 timed gaps per run that single stall sits at the maximum and does not move a 99th percentile. In three of the nine candidate runs and two of the nine control runs it is ABSENT, and p99 then climbs to whatever the next tail is: 72, 116, 157 ms. So p99 at this cell is bimodal on whether one stall lands in the window, and it is not measuring a policy.

findings.finding: The maximum gap shows no effect either, which retracts the other half of the earlier reading.
findings.detail: Median ratio 0.969, worse for the candidate in four of nine pairs. The earlier three-repeat reading -- that the policy converts one long stall into several medium ones, so max improves while p99 worsens -- was the same sampling seen from the other side. Neither direction survives nine repeats.
